position: Secretary of Labor; Wage and Hour Division; OSHA; Congress
proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL clarify that teleworking employees need to record time only when assigned work exceeds their usual amount, that a home office is not subject to OSHA regulations, that home-office setup time is not compensable, and that home-office expense reimbursements, even repeated ones such as internet or phone service, are not part of the regular rate; it also asks Congress to limit telework overtime to days over 10 hours (pp. 589 to 590).
remaining: Guidance that telework time need be recorded only above the usual daily workload (p. 590; none found)
Statement that a home office is not subject to OSHA regulations (p. 590; none found since 2025-01-20; any earlier OSHA home-office enforcement policy was not verified in this run)
Guidance that setup time is not compensable and that repeated home-office reimbursements are excluded from the regular rate (p. 590; none found)
Legislation limiting telework overtime to days over 10 hours (p. 589; none found)

status_summary: No DOL rule or guidance addressing the recordkeeping, OSHA home-office, setup-time or regular-rate clarifications was found. A Federal Register search of Labor Department documents for home office, telework and remote work since 2025-01-20 returned nothing. On 2026-07-22 the Wage and Hour Division issued opinion letters FLSA2026-9 and FLSA2026-10 on whether travel and work time between home and a work office is compensable, which touch hybrid work but not the listed clarifications. A trade-press report said the division head, asked in 2026 about remote-work stipends in the regular rate, answered that it depends on the details.
title: Clarify telework rules: home-office OSHA coverage, recordkeeping and regular rate
uncertainties: No DOL rule or guidance addressing telework recordkeeping, home-office OSHA coverage, setup time or regular-rate treatment of home-office reimbursements was found. The Labor Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) has no entry on these subjects, though such clarifications could come by opinion letter or field bulletin. Opinion letters FLSA2026-9 and FLSA2026-10 (2026-07-22) on travel between home and a work office touch hybrid work; their texts were not opened and the opinion letter search page was script-driven. No bill limiting telework overtime to days over 10 hours was found. An earlier OSHA home-office policy predates the window. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
